input.summary: On the 1972 Bally Fireball, learn the 3K plunge, keep one ball in Wotan when possible, and repeat the Wotan gate instead of forcing uncontrolled three-ball play.

quickInfo.name: 3K skill shot
quickInfo.summary: Plunge just short of the upper-left gate to cross the horizontal 1K lanes and light the three bumpers.

quickInfo.name: Odin and Wotan locks
quickInfo.summary: Each saucer lock gives another plunge, while a side mushroom bumper releases the ball from the opposite saucer.

quickInfo.name: Zip flippers
quickInfo.summary: The center mushroom closes the gap between the flippers, while the side mushrooms can open it again.

quickInfo.name: Wotan gate
quickInfo.summary: With a ball in Wotan, another Wotan shot passes through the gate and scores the lit mushroom-bumper values.

quickInfo.name: Three-ball play
quickInfo.summary: Releasing locked balls creates multiball without a Jackpot objective, so new locks and plunges remain the priority.

quickInfo.name: Edition scope
quickInfo.summary: This route and image cover the original 1972 Bally electromechanical Fireball with zipper flippers.

steps.text: Plunge so the ball stops before the upper-left gate. Let it fall across the horizontal 1K lanes.
Use the plunge to light the mushroom bumpers. Treat each later lock as another skill-shot chance.
Use the center mushroom to zip the flippers when the hit is available through normal play.
Settle the ball on the zipped flippers. Micro flip the ball up the opposite flipper.
Backhand Odin or Wotan to lock a ball. Prefer Wotan when both saucers are available.
With one ball held in Wotan, repeat the Wotan shot. Let the moving ball pass the gate and score the lit bumper values.
modeNotes: Wotan gate loop: The held ball blocks the saucer. The next ball passes through the gate and crosses the upper rollovers before it returns.
Lock value: Each lock also gives a new plunge and another chance at the 3K skill shot.

steps.text: If a side mushroom releases the held ball, relock a ball as soon as control permits. Do not chase three-ball chaos for its own sake.

fallback.title: Lock and plunge
fallback.when: Use this when the Wotan repeat gate is unreliable or the zipped-flipper settle does not work.

steps.text: Shoot the safer lock saucer from a controlled flipper.
Use the new plunge for the 3K skill shot.
Relight the bumpers and accept their incidental scoring.
Relock the returned ball when either saucer shot is controlled.

alternatives.title: Controlled multiball recovery
alternatives.when: Use this after a side mushroom releases a locked ball.

steps.text: Keep the flippers zipped when the ball paths permit it.
Do not flip at a ball that can settle on the zipped flippers.
Use short flips to separate the balls.
Return one ball to Odin or Wotan before you resume gate loops.
Plunge the lit upper lane to light the mushroom bumpers.
Zip the flippers and lock one ball in Wotan.
Repeat the Wotan gate while the lock remains held.
Restore the Wotan lock after each multiball release.

playfieldReferences.label: Wotan lock and gate
playfieldReferences.description: The right saucer whose occupied lock lets another Wotan shot pass through the scoring gate.

playfieldReferences.label: Odin lock saucer
playfieldReferences.description: The left saucer used to hold a ball and earn another plunge.

playfieldReferences.label: Zip-flipper mushroom
playfieldReferences.description: The center mushroom bumper that closes the gap between the flippers.

playfieldReferences.label: Spinning playfield disk
playfieldReferences.description: The rotating rubber disk that can redirect a ball unpredictably.

techniques.name: Backhand
techniques.instruction: From a zipped cradle, Micro flip the ball up the opposite flipper, then Backhand Wotan from halfway up that flipper.

techniques.name: Cradle
techniques.instruction: When the flippers are zipped, let a centered ball settle without a flip. Use a small flip only after the ball stops.

cautions.issue: Most non-saucer shots can rebound without control.
cautions.response: Prefer saucer backhands. Trap the ball before each planned lock shot.

cautions.issue: The spinning rubber disk can hold a ball briefly and then throw it in a new direction.
cautions.response: Keep both flippers ready when the ball crosses the disk. Do not predict a clean feed from its first contact.

cautions.issue: Top-bumper feeds can return at high speed and start uncontrolled multiball.
cautions.response: Do not force a side-mushroom release. Rebuild one useful lock after the balls separate.

checkBeforePlay: Confirm the original 1972 Bally Fireball, not Fireball Classic or another edition, plus ball count, replay, award conversion, and tilt.
Confirm plunge scoring, both lock and release switches, Wotan gate values, mushroom-bumper lights, zip-flipper action, and whether Special has tournament value.
Test both saucer backhands, gate return, side-mushroom releases, spinning-disk exits, zipped-flipper settle, and plunge strength before choosing the Wotan loop.
input.simpleOverview: Fireball uses each saucer lock to give another plunge, while a ball held in Wotan turns later Wotan shots into a repeatable gate loop. Make the 3K plunge, close the zipper flippers, store one ball in Wotan, and repeat its gate while the lock remains held.
input.overview: Fireball uses each saucer lock to give another plunge, while a ball held in Wotan turns later Wotan shots into a repeatable gate loop. Favor a held Wotan ball and repeated Wotan-gate scoring over uncontrolled three-ball play, restoring the lock after any release and using each new lock for another plunge.
